extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, inventors, assignees, patent practitioners/agents, and third parties seeking access to USPTO application files or Board records
extracted.subtask_short: access and confidentiality of patent files
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria governing when and how patent application files, provisional files, reissue/reexamination files, PTAB records, and international PCT files may be accessed or disclosed to the public or to specific persons, and the authorization/petition/FOIA requirements for obtaining access. Covers powers to inspect, petitions for access, Director/Board publication, and FOIA/international confidentiality limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of unpublished patent applications (37 CFR 1.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning the filing, pendency, or subject matter of an application for patent, including status information, and access to the application, will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline rule: unpublished applications are confidential except as specifically authorized by statute or the regulations (e.g., 37 CFR 1.11, 1.14). Any public access must conform to the exceptions enumerated in 1.14(a)(1) or other paragraphs of 1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unpublished abandoned applications identified or relied upon (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file contents of an unpublished, abandoned application may be made available to the public if the application is identified in a U.S. patent, a statutory invention registration, a U.S. patent application publication, an international publication under PCT Article 21(2), or a publication under Hague Agreement Article 10(3). An application is considered identified when application number/serial and filing date, first named inventor, title, and filing date or other application-specific information are provided in the text of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document may be provided upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)). Identification in a paper within the file contents (but not in the printed patent) does not suffice. This rule applies to provisional applications relied upon for priority once the relying document is published/issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the file contents of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)), if the benefit of the application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) in an application that has issued as a U.S. patent or has published (patent application publication, statutory invention registration, international publication, or Hague publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) (power to inspect) or (i) (petitions) of 37 CFR 1.14. Copies provided may be the application-as-filed or specific documents from the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unpublished pending applications incorporated by reference or otherwise identified (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application as originally filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)), if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, international publication under PCT Article 21(2), or Hague Article 10(3) publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with (iv) and (v), the Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) (power to inspect) or (i) (petitions). The availability is limited to copies of the application-as-filed or specific documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a petition for access or a power to inspect is required (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that were not published or patented, or that are not otherwise identified in public documents, are not available to the public unless a granted petition for access (see paragraph (i)) or a power to inspect (see paragraph (c)) is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier-filed application is only identified in the file contents of another application (but not in the published patent/publication itself), a petition for access or power to inspect is necessary. See MPEP §1002.02(b), item 21 for handling; petitions are handled in the Office of Patent Legal Administration unless the application is involved in certain proceedings (interference, derivation, PTAB trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for access requirements and process (37 CFR 1.14(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition by a member of the public seeking access to, or copies of, all or part of any pending or abandoned application preserved in confidence must include: (1) the fee set forth in § 1.17(g); and (2) a showing that access is necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or that special circumstances exist which warrant access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should include complete identification of petitioner (including post office address with ZIP, telephone, facsimile) to expedite handling. Petition may be filed with proof of service on inventor/applicant/assignee/attorney of record, or filed in duplicate (duplicate sent to applicant by Office). A separate petition and fee are required for each application. Petitions should explain why access is desired and why petitioner believes they are entitled to access. Applicant normally given a limited period (e.g., 3 weeks) to state objections; if applicant consents, petition granted; if objection or no response, petition decided on the record. If access granted, applicant’s objections in the file become available to petitioner; if denied, petitioner will not receive copies of applicant’s objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and examples of "special circumstances" justifying petition access
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination whether "special circumstances" are present will be made; examples include where an applicant has relied on the applicant's application to interfere with a competitor’s business or customers, or where an attorney/agent of record in one application lacks power of attorney in a copending application having a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such special circumstances exist, the Director may grant access under 35 U.S.C. 122. In some cases, obtaining a power to inspect from an assignee or inventor may be a more expeditious means of obtaining access than a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to inspect—who may sign (applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012) (37 CFR 1.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access may be provided if the application file contains written authority (power to inspect) signed by: (1) the applicant; (2) a patent practitioner of record; (3) the assignee or an assignee of an undivided part interest; (4) the inventor or a joint inventor; or (5) a registered attorney or agent named in the papers accompanying the application (if a power of attorney has not been appointed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written authority must identify the application and the name of the person authorized to have access and will be made of record. Access provided upon the written order of the Director will also become part of the record. A person acting in representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 may execute a power to inspect only if the patent practitioner was named in application transmittal papers and no power of attorney has been appointed; once a power of attorney is filed, previously filed powers by practitioner without POA cease to have effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to inspect—who may sign (applications filed before Sept 16, 2012) (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-September 16, 2012 applications, the written authority must be signed by: (1) an applicant; (2) an attorney or agent of record; (3) an authorized official of an assignee of record; or (4) a registered attorney or agent named in the papers accompanying the application (if an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63/1.497 has not been filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an executed oath or declaration has been filed for pre-2012 applications, only the applicant (any one of joint applicants), an attorney or agent of record (if a power of attorney was filed), or an assignee whose assignment is of record will be permitted to have access, unless written authority from one of those parties or a Director order is made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to inspect—form, scope, and specificity required
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to inspect must specifically name the person entitled to inspect and copy the application, must specifically identify the application by application number, and be limited to a single application. Form PTO/SB/67 may be used for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An associate or representative of the named person is not entitled to access on behalf of the authorized person. The written authorization will be entered as part of the official file. In provisional applications, because no oath/declaration is required there may be no power of attorney in the application; certified copies will be supplied to the correspondence address if requester is not a named inventor/applicant/assignee/attorney of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers to inspect not accepted in Image File Wrapper (IFW) / access via Private PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers to inspect are not accepted in Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications. IFW applications are available through Private PAIR and attorneys/applicants of record have direct access when a Customer Number is associated and they have Private PAIR access. IFW published application or patent files are available through Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant/inventor/assignee/attorney cannot view an IFW application through Private PAIR or Patent Center, a copy must be purchased from the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch of the Public Records Division. A "power to inspect" is effectively the same as a "power to inspect and make copies."

rubrics_metrics.name: Access on oral request and identity proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Access will be given on oral request to any applicant, inventor, patentee, assignee, or attorney or agent of record in an application or patent only upon proof of identity or upon recognition based on personal acquaintance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where power of attorney or authorization was given to a registered firm prior to July 2, 1971, access will be given on oral request to any registered member or employee of the firm who has signatory power. Unregistered employees, public stenographers, and others not within these provisions will be given access only upon presentation of a written authorization (power to inspect) signed by an authorized person and entered as part of the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications are generally preserved in confidence and access/copies are customarily only made available under the limited circumstances provided in 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv)-(vi) and 1.14(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certified copies or access via power to inspect, the requester must have written authority from a named inventor, applicant, assignee of record, or the attorney or agent of record, unless the provisional application is otherwise available per the cited regulatory exceptions. If requester is not a named inventor/applicant/assignee/attorney of record, the certified copy will be supplied to the correspondence address of the provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspended or excluded practitioner cannot inspect
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees are forbidden to hold either oral or written communication with an attorney or agent who has been suspended or excluded from practice by the USPTO regarding an application unless that attorney/agent is an inventor or the applicant. Power to inspect given to such an attorney or agent will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute restriction to prevent acceptance of powers to inspect from practitioners suspended/excluded from practice, except where they are inventors or applicants themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of inspection by assignee and inventor rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or assignee of record of the entire interest may file or intervene and appoint counsel of choice; such filing or intervention does not exclude the inventor from access unless the applicant or assignee files a separate paper requesting prevention of the inventor's access (37 CFR 1.4(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to prevent the inventor from obtaining access should be directed to the Office of Petitions and, if granted, inventor will only be permitted to inspect upon sufficient showing why such inspection is necessary to conserve his/her rights. After the application publishes under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the application becomes available to the public and any previous restriction on inventor access ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of assignee of part interest to inspect
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of a part interest or a licensee of an exclusive right is entitled to inspect the application, even though only an assignee of the entire interest may intervene to exclude the applicant from prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For details on prosecution by an assignee, see MPEP §§ 324 (pre-Sept 16, 2012) and 325 (post-Sept 16, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive publications—public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire application file of a defensive publication is available to the public for inspection and obtaining copies (see MPEP § 711.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive-publication application files are treated as open files and are available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications—public inspection and Patent Center access (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.11(b) opens reissue applications to inspection by the general public and provides for announcement of filings of reissue applications in the Official Gazette (with exceptions). IFW reissue application files are open to inspection by the general public via Patent Center and members of the public will be able to view the entire content of the reissue application file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Official Gazette gives the public an opportunity to submit information pertinent to patentability of the reissue application to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination files—publication of filing and access timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An announcement of the filing of each request for reexamination in which the entire fee has been paid, and of each reexamination ordered by the Director, will be published in the Official Gazette. A reexamination file is normally NOT open to inspection by the general public until the file has been scanned into the IFW system, at which point the file is open via Patent Center. In viewing reexamination images, members of the public will be able to view the entire contents of the reexamination file with the exception of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2232 for further details about reexamination file content and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decisions—publication criteria and applicant protections (37 CFR 1.14(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision by the Director that would not otherwise be open to public inspection may be published or made available for public inspection if: (1) the Director believes the decision involves an interpretation of patent laws or regulations that would be of precedential value; and (2) the applicant is given notice and an opportunity to object in writing within two months on the ground that the decision discloses a trade secret or other confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any objection must identify deletions necessary to protect the information or explain why the entire decision must be withheld. An applicant or party will be given not less than twenty days to request reconsideration and seek court review before portions of a decision are made public under this paragraph over his or her objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB records and Board action publication (37 CFR 41.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) Any Board action is available for public inspection without a party’s permission if rendered in a file open to the public pursuant to § 1.11 or in an application that has been published. The Office may independently publish any Board action that is available for public inspection. (2) Board actions not publishable under (a)(1) may be published if the Director believes special circumstances warrant publication and a party does not object in writing within two months on trade secret/confidentiality grounds; the party must identify deletions necessary and will have at least twenty days for reconsideration and court review before contested portions are made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b)(1) The record of a Board proceeding is available to the public unless a patent application not otherwise available to the public is involved. (b)(2) After a final Board action or judgment, the record will be made available if any involved file becomes open under § 1.11 or the application is published. These provisions mirror Director decision protections and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA request requirements for USPTO records (37 CFR 102.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for USPTO records not customarily made available must be in writing and will be processed under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). For quickest handling, mark the request letter and envelope "Freedom of Information Act Request." For requests for records about another individual, either a written authorization signed by that individual or proof that the individual is deceased facilitates processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must describe the records with enough detail to enable USPTO personnel to locate them (date, title/name, author, recipient, subject matter, office location). If the FOIA Officer determines the request does not reasonably describe records, the Officer will inform the requester what additional information is needed or may offer an opportunity to discuss and modify the request. See 37 CFR Part 102, Subpart A, and USPTO e-FOIA resources for further rules and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential nature of international (PCT) applications and preliminary examination (PCT Articles 30 & 38; 35 U.S.C. 368)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to specified provisos, the International Bureau and International Searching/Preliminary Examining Authorities shall not allow access to the international application or preliminary examination file before international publication unless requested or authorized by the applicant. No national Office shall allow access to the international application by third parties before the earliest of the international publication date, receipt of Article 20 communication, or receipt of a copy under Article 22. Access covers any means by which third parties may acquire cognizance, and national Offices generally shall not publish the international application or its translation before international publication or, if not published by 20 months, before 20 months from priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited data (receiving Office identification, applicant name, international filing date, international application number, and title) may be published earlier. Where the U.S. acts as Receiving Office, copies of international application files published under PCT Article 21(2) will be furnished in accordance with PCT Articles and Rules upon written request showing publication and designation of the U.S., and upon payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).
